skill.name: project-to-obsidian
skill.description: Convert code projects into structured Obsidian knowledge bases with linked notes, architecture views, API references, and module documentation.
skill.summary: Generate linked Obsidian documentation from a code project after user confirmation.
skill.author: Claude Code

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, slash-command examples, Obsidian links, Mermaid diagrams, and normal Claude skill installation instructions. I confirmed the .env and configuration scanning guidance because it can expose credentials when generated notes capture environment values. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration language was found.

remediation.issue: Default scan pattern includes environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Remove **/.env* from default scans, or require explicit confirmation before reading secret-bearing files.

remediation.issue: Generated configuration notes may disclose secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Document variable names only and redact tokens, passwords, keys, connection strings, and private URLs before writing notes.

remediation.issue: Project scanning mentions shell-based ls/find usage.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Glob and read-only file APIs, or use hardcoded safe commands without interpolating user paths.

content.user_title: Convert Projects into Obsidian Knowledge Bases
content.value_statement: Project knowledge is often scattered across code, comments, and docs. This skill turns a codebase into linked Obsidian notes for navigation and maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Scans project structure and identifies common language, framework, and configuration markers.
Generates project overview, quickstart, architecture, API, module, configuration, and developer guide notes.
Creates Obsidian wikilinks, tags, properties, Dataview indexes, and Mermaid diagrams.
Supports output to an Obsidian vault, local folder, or project docs directory after confirmation.
Provides reusable templates for API endpoints, modules, architecture, quickstart, and project overview.
limitations: It may read configuration files, so users should redact secrets before use.
Direct vault writes depend on available Obsidian MCP tools.
Large repositories may need quick mode or a narrower project path.
Generated documentation should be reviewed before sharing or publishing.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Create a linked overview of structure, dependencies, entry points, and major modules.

use_cases.title: Prepare architecture review notes
use_cases.description: Generate architecture summaries, Mermaid diagrams, and module relationships for technical review.

use_cases.title: Refresh project documentation
use_cases.description: Build or update Obsidian notes for APIs, modules, quickstart steps, and configuration references.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Quick Project Overview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan for a small project.
prompt_templates.prompt: /p2o ./my-project --quick and create a local folder. Ask before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Generate API Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: /p2o ./backend --api. Focus on routes, request parameters, response shapes, and linked API notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Architecture Vault
prompt_templates.prompt: /p2o ./platform --arch. Use Mermaid diagrams, module links, and a short decisions summary.

prompt_templates.title: Create Full Obsidian Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced full conversion with safer boundaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert ./monorepo into an Obsidian knowledge base. Exclude secrets, generated files, and dependencies. Output to my selected vault path.

output_examples.input: User requests a quick overview for a TypeScript service.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a project overview, directory structure note, technology stack note, and links between key modules.

output_examples.input: User requests API documentation for a backend.
output_examples.output: The skill creates endpoint notes with methods, parameters, responses, source file references, and related module links.

output_examples.input: User requests full Obsidian vault output.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for confirmation, creates a project knowledge base, adds indexes, and writes linked notes to the chosen destination.

best_practices: Confirm the project path and output location before scanning or writing.
Exclude secret, dependency, build, and generated files from documentation.
Review generated notes before moving them from an AI inbox into shared vault sections.
anti_patterns: Do not point the skill at a home directory or broad filesystem root.
Do not publish generated configuration notes without checking for secrets.
Do not overwrite existing Obsidian notes without a review step.

faq.question: Does this write directly to Obsidian?
faq.answer: It can write through Obsidian MCP when available. It can also create a local folder or project docs directory after confirmation.

faq.question: Which languages and frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: It recognizes JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and common framework markers. Templates can adapt to other projects.

faq.question: Does it execute project code?
faq.answer: It is intended to inspect files and structure, not run the application. Users should decline unexpected commands.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Exclude or redact environment files and secret configuration before generation. Review configuration notes before sharing them.

faq.question: Can it update existing notes?
faq.answer: The workflow prefers append and patch operations in an AI inbox. Review changes before moving notes into shared vault sections.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. File and vault access depend on the active tool environment.
